title: The Broken Playlist
premise: At Ashgrove Academy, every senior must answer the annual 'Honesty Essay' prompt, read aloud anonymously at Founders' Assembly — a tradition that has quietly decided scholarships, reputations, and futures for a century. Elodie Brightwater, a scholarship student who has spent twelve years perfecting invisibility, writes the truth about the academy's founder and the town fortune built on her great-grandmother's stolen music, never expecting it to be traced back to them. When their essay ignites a war between the founding families who profit from the tradition and the students it silences, Elodie must choose between the safe, careful life they've built and claiming an inheritance of song, grief, and power. The story ends at prom, where Elodie restores the broken playlist of the founder's erased collaborator, exposes the corruption propping up the academy, and accepts that being seen is the only survival that counts.
about_author: Hazel Coldharbour is the pen name of a former boarding-school scholarship kid who now writes stories about institutions, inheritance, and the teenagers who survive both. They live in a coastal town full of old money and older secrets, where they collect vinyl records they refuse to alphabetize.

chapters.title: The Prompt
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Senior year begins at Ashgrove Academy with the announcement of this year's Honesty Essay prompt: 'What have you never said out loud?' Elodie, on scholarship and perpetually careful, catalogs everyone's fear while hiding their own. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath practiced composure.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Careful
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Flashbacks interweave with present-day scenes as Elodie navigates lunchroom hierarchies, tutoring rich classmate Julian Vance, and avoiding the attention of Headmistress Crane. We learn why visibility has always meant danger for Elodie's family. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: The Founder's Portrait
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Researching the essay in the archive, Elodie discovers gaps in the school's official history: Augusta Ashgrove's celebrated compositions list no co-writer, though marginalia hints at one. A librarian, Ms. Okonkwo, slips Elodie a key to the restricted stacks. Emotional beat: first spark of curiosity over caution.

chapters.title: Julian's Confession
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian drafts his essay about his father's expectations and hates how safe it sounds. He watches Elodie, envies their apparent freedom from his family's name, and engineers a study partnership. Emotional beat: envy curdling into fascination.

chapters.title: What the Stacks Keep
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. In the restricted stacks, Elodie finds letters between Augusta Ashgrove and Delphine Brightwater — Elodie's great-grandmother, a Black composer whose melodies Augusta published under her own name. Elodie's hands shake. Emotional beat: vertigo of inherited erasure.

chapters.title: The Draft
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie writes the Honesty Essay in one furious night: the theft, the family silence, the twelve years of careful. Then panic — anonymity is promised, but nothing at Ashgrove stays anonymous. They almost burn it. Emotional beat: rage wrestling with terror.

chapters.title: Submission
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Essays are sealed; the whole senior class speculates. Crane announces the readings will be 'curated' by the Board of Trustees — a new rule. Elodie notices the seal on their envelope already broken. Emotional beat: dread arriving ahead of consequences.

chapters.title: Assembly
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Three essays are read aloud, each one defanged. Then a fourth voice reads words Elodie recognizes as their own — but altered, softened, stripped of names. Someone knows. Whispers begin. Emotional beat: exposure without acknowledgment, the worst kind.

chapters.title: Crane's Offer
chapters.summary: Headmistress Crane's POV. Crane privately offers Elodie a full-ride renewal and a letter of recommendation in exchange for silence about the archive findings. She reveals she knows exactly whose great-granddaughter Elodie is. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a kind face.

chapters.title: The Vance Fortune
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian learns his family's wealth traces to publishing rights Augusta stole alongside the music — his father sits on the Board. He confronts his father and gets a lesson in how power keeps itself. Emotional beat: disillusionment as inheritance.

chapters.title: Allies and Leaks
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie and Julian form an uneasy alliance, joined by Priya Raghavan, student council president, whose own essay was suppressed last year. But someone leaks Elodie's original essay text online, and the school blames Elodie for 'instability.' Emotional beat: solidarity forged under fire.

chapters.title: Delphine's Box
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie visits their grandmother, who finally opens the family box: Delphine's notebooks, an unreleased recording, and a broken playlist reel labeled 'For Augusta, when she finds her courage.' Grandma reveals why the family chose silence — survival once required it. Emotional beat: grief becoming fuel.

chapters.title: The Tradition Questioned
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Student body fractures: some demand the essay tradition end entirely, others defend it as sacred. Board members visit classrooms, smiling threats. Priya proposes the seniors read their own essays, unedited, at prom. Emotional beat: courage spreading like contagion.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian's father threatens to revoke the Vances' funding, which would kill the prom and the reading plan. Julian's scholarship-style dependence mirrors Elodie's. He chooses his father's money over the alliance — publicly. Emotional beat: betrayal by someone who understands.

chapters.title: Invisible Again
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. With Julian gone and Crane tightening control, Elodie retreats into old habits, nearly withdrawing from school. Ms. Okonkwo is dismissed for 'archive irregularities.' Elodie realizes invisibility was never safety — just a slower surrender. Emotional beat: rock bottom, then refusal.

chapters.title: The Recording
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Listening to Delphine's recording, Elodie hears Augusta's voice at the end, young and ashamed, promising credit 'when it's safe.' It never was. Elodie decides the essay tradition can be saved only by making it honest again. Emotional beat: purpose crystallizing from pain.

chapters.title: Rebuilding the Alliance
chapters.summary: Priya and Elodie's POV. Elodie forgives Julian — not for his sake, but because the movement needs everyone's shame made useful. Julian agrees to testify about the Board's finances. They plan to hijack prom's sound system with Delphine's playlist. Emotional beat: fragile, chosen trust.

chapters.title: Prom Eve
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Crane discovers the plan and locks down the gym, cancels the DJ, and threatens expulsions. The Board votes to end the essay tradition permanently — burying it rather than fixing it. Everything hinges on one unguarded door and one borrowed laptop. Emotional beat: held breath.

chapters.title: The Broken Playlist
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Climax. During prom, Elodie takes the stage, plays Delphine's music, and reads their essay unedited — naming Augusta, naming Delphine, naming themselves. Students stand one by one, reading their own suppressed truths. Crane cuts the power; the room sings the chorus from memory. Emotional beat: catharsis, loud and irreversible.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. The fallout: trustees resign, an independent audit begins, Okonkwo is reinstated, and Julian's father faces the publishers' ledger. Julian publicly renounces his inheritance's dirty portion. Emotional beat: accountability as a beginning, not an ending.

chapters.title: What Survives
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Crane resigns; an interim headmistress asks Elodie what the tradition should become. Elodie proposes essays read aloud, always, by their authors, with the archive renamed for Delphine Brightwater. Elodie is accepted to college — on merit, with an essay they're proud of. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, epilogue. Graduation. Elodie places Delphine's restored playlist in the archive beside Augusta's portrait, both finally credited together. Walking across the stage, Elodie is fully visible and no longer afraid. Final line echoes the prompt: some things you say out loud so they can outlive you. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed, future open.
